# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

I read the code and found nothing wrong with the technical basics. It's a small Next.js site with 3 public pages and 1 private page. The scored rules all come back clear, and no result depends on something outside the code. Whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through is the one thing code can't show. The score doesn't include it.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Confirm real crawlers can reach the site
- **Why it matters:** Your code allows search crawlers, but a CDN or firewall in front of the site could still block them. Code can't show that.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` followed by `Allow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100 if it comes back clear. The score stays 100 if it comes back as a problem, because this check isn't a scored rule. It would show up as a separate finding.

Run `geopilot logs <your access log file>`. It compares the crawlers in your server logs with the addresses their operators publish.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is reachable and valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny file |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says they should | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Search crawlers fall under `*` and are allowed. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 public routes have no noindex. `/account` has noindex on purpose and isn't in the sitemap. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1` |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in server HTML | Clear | Server Components, text is in the page code |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD in the project |
| GEO-011 | Valid sitemap that can be discovered | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml`, and `public/robots.txt:11` has an absolute `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. 3 of 3 public routes have a title and description. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable through real links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:7` uses `<a href>` for all 3 pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | No page-wide `nosnippet`. `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:9` covers one element only, which is fine. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Read the layout and 4 pages. There are no images, and the links have text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not present. It isn't scored. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not an app. It isn't scored. |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Deliver the "directions" the Visit page promises:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`. The page body only says `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` Adding an address, directions and opening hours as text would match the description. You could then label them with LocalBusiness structured data.
- **Back up the "Over forty varieties" claim:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` Only two names appear. A list would let readers and machines see the rest.
- **Give each variety its own page:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`. A list of 40+ varieties could have a page and address for each, such as `/varieties/ashmeads-kernel`. Each could then be linked and added to the sitemap.
- **State who the site is from in a machine-readable way:** `app/layout.tsx:1`: `metadataBase: new URL('https://www.orchard.example')`. No Organization or WebSite structured data names the orchard or links to it. You could add it in the layout.
- **Add a site-wide default title and description:** `app/layout.tsx:1`. The layout sets only `metadataBase`, so a new page that forgets its own metadata would have no title or description.
- **Add `<lastmod>` dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.orchard.example/</loc></url>`. If you know when pages last changed, dates could help crawlers decide what to re-fetch.
- **Link between related pages:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.` The home page text could link to Varieties and Visit, and Varieties could link to Visit.
- **Keep the site URL in one place:** `geo.config.json` and `app/layout.tsx:1` each state `https://www.orchard.example`, and every page's canonical repeats it. If the domain changes, all of them need editing. A shared constant would avoid that.
- **Make the descriptions more specific:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Over forty heritage apple varieties.'`. Mentioning that it's a Herefordshire orchard would say who the page is from and where.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live-only checks:** real status codes, redirects, `X-Robots-Tag` headers and whether the sitemap URLs answer 200 need a live scan. Give me the URL if you want one.
- **Training crawlers:** `public/robots.txt:5-9` blocks GPTBot and ClaudeBot. That matches your `trainingCrawlers: "block"` policy, so I haven't counted it.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find the public pages. `geo.config.json` says so with `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- `/account` is private on purpose. It has noindex, a `Disallow` rule and no sitemap entry, so I left it out of the sampled routes and didn't count its missing description.
- `https://www.orchard.example` is the real domain, as declared in `geo.config.json`.

## What to do next

1. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to confirm real crawlers get through (item 1).
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
